dishes.desc: Marinated pork or lamb chunks grilled on skewers over charcoal, a summer dacha tradition.

dishes.name: Vareniki
dishes.desc: Boiled dumplings filled with potato, cottage cheese or cherries, served with sour cream.

dishes.name: Medovik
dishes.desc: Layered honey cake of thin honey-flavoured sponge sheets and sour-cream frosting.

dishes.name: Kvass
dishes.desc: Fermented low-alcohol drink of rye bread, slightly sour and sweet, sold from street barrels in summer.

dishes.name: Zefir
dishes.desc: Airy confection of whipped fruit purée, sugar and egg whites set with pectin, similar to marshmallow.

dishes.name: Pryaniki
dishes.desc: Spiced honey gingerbread cookies, often glazed or stamped, most famously from Tula.

dishes.name: Ukha
dishes.desc: Clear soup of freshwater fish with root vegetables and herbs, sometimes laced with vodka.

dishes.name: Golubtsy
dishes.desc: Cabbage rolls of minced meat and rice stewed in a tomato and sour-cream sauce.

dishes.name: Vinegret
dishes.desc: Salad of diced beetroot, potatoes, carrots, pickles and sauerkraut dressed with sunflower oil.

dishes.name: Tvorog
dishes.desc: Fresh farmer's cheese eaten with sour cream, sugar or jam, and used in many desserts.

dishes.name: Syrnaya Paskha
dishes.desc: Pyramid-shaped Easter dessert of tvorog, butter, cream and raisins, moulded with religious symbols.

dishes.name: Kholodets
dishes.desc: Meat jelly of slow-boiled pork or beef set in aspic, served cold with mustard or horseradish at holidays.

dishes.name: Vodka
dishes.desc: Clear distilled spirit of grain or potatoes, drunk chilled in shots alongside zakuski.

dishes.name: Kefir
dishes.desc: Tangy fermented milk drink made with kefir grains, drunk at breakfast and before bed.

dishes.name: Kulich
dishes.desc: Tall Easter bread with raisins and candied peel under white icing, blessed at church.

dishes.name: Cepelinai
dishes.desc: Large zeppelin-shaped grated-potato dumplings stuffed with minced meat, served with sour cream and bacon.

dishes.name: Šaltibarščiai
dishes.desc: Bright pink cold beetroot soup with kefir, cucumber and dill, served with hot boiled potatoes.

dishes.name: Kibinai
dishes.desc: Crescent pastries filled with mutton or other meat and onion, a Karaim specialty from Trakai.

dishes.name: Šakotis
dishes.desc: Spiky tree cake made by dripping egg-rich batter onto a rotating spit over an open fire.

dishes.name: Kugelis
dishes.desc: Baked grated-potato pudding with bacon and onions, served with sour cream.

dishes.name: Skilandis
dishes.desc: Cold-smoked minced pork and fat stuffed into a pig's stomach, aged and served thinly sliced.

dishes.name: Balandėliai
dishes.desc: Cabbage leaves stuffed with minced meat and rice, stewed in tomato or sour-cream sauce.

dishes.name: Koldūnai
dishes.desc: Small dumplings filled with minced meat or curd cheese, served with butter or sour cream.

dishes.name: Bulviniai Blynai
dishes.desc: Grated potato pancakes fried in oil, served with sour cream or apple sauce.

dishes.name: Kepta Duona
dishes.desc: Strips of dark rye bread fried in oil and rubbed with garlic, served with a cheese dip alongside beer.

dishes.name: Vėdarai
dishes.desc: Pig intestines stuffed with grated potato and bacon, baked until crisp.

dishes.name: Šaltanosiai
dishes.desc: Small dumplings filled with lingonberries or bilberries, served with sour cream and sugar.

dishes.name: Grybukai
dishes.desc: Mushroom-shaped honey-spice cookies with white icing caps and poppy-seed-dipped stems.

dishes.name: Kūčiukai
dishes.desc: Small crunchy poppy-seed biscuits eaten soaked in poppy milk on Christmas Eve (Kūčios).

dishes.name: Midus
dishes.desc: Traditional mead fermented from honey, sometimes spiced with herbs, one of the oldest Lithuanian drinks.

dishes.name: Skruzdėlynas
dishes.desc: Anthill cake of fried dough pieces piled into a mound and drizzled with honey and poppy seeds.

dishes.name: Grey Peas with Bacon
dishes.desc: Boiled grey peas fried with smoked bacon and onions, served with kefir, a Christmas and everyday classic.

dishes.name: Rupjmaize
dishes.desc: Dense dark rye bread made from coarse wholegrain flour, often with caraway, baked in wood-fired ovens.

dishes.name: Rasols
dishes.desc: Pink potato salad with beetroot, pickles, meat or herring, eggs and a sour-cream dressing; festive fare.

dishes.name: Speķa Pīrādziņi
dishes.desc: Crescent-shaped yeast buns filled with chopped bacon and onion, baked for holidays.

dishes.name: Rye Bread Dessert (Rupjmaizes Kārtojums)
dishes.desc: Layered dessert of grated sweetened rye bread, whipped cream and cranberry or lingonberry jam.

dishes.name: Sklandrausis
dishes.desc: Open rye-crust tart filled with mashed potato and sweet carrot, a Couronian speciality.

dishes.name: Kartupeļu Pankūkas
dishes.desc: Grated potato pancakes fried golden, served with sour cream or lingonberry jam.

dishes.name: Zivju Zupa
dishes.desc: Clear fish soup of salmon or local fish with potatoes, carrots and dill.

dishes.name: Skābeņu Zupa
dishes.desc: Sorrel soup with potatoes and boiled egg, sometimes with pork, served with sour cream.

dishes.name: Biezpiena Sieriņš
dishes.desc: Chilled sweet curd-cheese bar coated in chocolate, a popular snack.

dishes.name: Siers ar Ķimenēm
dishes.desc: Fresh caraway-seed cheese, known as Jāņu siers, made for the Midsummer (Jāņi) celebrations.

dishes.name: Riga Sprats (Šprotes)
dishes.desc: Small Baltic sprats cold-smoked and preserved in oil in tins, eaten on rye bread.

dishes.name: Black Balsam
dishes.desc: Bitter black herbal liqueur from Riga made with dozens of botanicals, drunk neat or in coffee.

dishes.name: Aukstā Zupa
dishes.desc: Cold summer beetroot soup with kefir, cucumber, dill and boiled egg.

dishes.name: Debesmanna
dishes.desc: Whipped pink semolina pudding cooked with cranberry or lingonberry juice, served with cold milk.

dishes.name: Ķiploku Grauzdiņi
dishes.desc: Fried strips of dark rye bread rubbed with garlic, the classic Latvian beer snack, often with cheese sauce.

dishes.name: Verivorst
dishes.desc: Blood sausage with barley, baked and served with lingonberry jam and sauerkraut at Christmas.

dishes.name: Mulgipuder
dishes.desc: Mash of potatoes and barley groats topped with fried pork and onion, from the Mulgimaa region.

dishes.name: Black Bread
dishes.desc: Dark sourdough rye bread (rukkileib), the staple eaten with almost every meal.

dishes.name: Kama
dishes.desc: Mixed flour of roasted barley, rye, oat and pea, stirred into kefir or buttermilk as a drink or dessert.

dishes.name: Kohuke
dishes.desc: Chocolate-glazed sweet curd-cheese snack bar, often flavoured with vanilla or fruit, sold chilled in shops.

dishes.name: Sült
dishes.desc: Jellied pork in aspic, served cold with mustard, especially at Christmas.

dishes.name: Kiluvoileib
dishes.desc: Rye bread open sandwich with marinated Baltic sprats, boiled egg and herbs.

dishes.name: Rosolje
dishes.desc: Pink beetroot and potato salad with herring, pickles and a sour-cream mayonnaise dressing.

dishes.name: Karask
dishes.desc: Quick barley-flour bread leavened with baking soda and kefir, sometimes with bacon.

dishes.name: Hapukapsas
dishes.desc: Sauerkraut stewed with pork and barley, served with blood sausage at Christmas.

dishes.name: Vastlakukkel
dishes.desc: Cardamom bun filled with whipped cream and jam, eaten on Shrove Tuesday.

dishes.name: Kali
dishes.desc: Fermented low-alcohol drink of rye bread and malt, similar to kvass.

dishes.name: Marzipan
dishes.desc: Almond and sugar confection, which Tallinn claims to have invented, sold as painted figurines.

dishes.name: Šašlõkk
dishes.desc: Marinated pork skewers grilled over charcoal, a must at Midsummer gatherings.

dishes.name: Suitsukala
dishes.desc: Hot-smoked fish such as flounder, perch or Baltic herring, sold on Saaremaa and along the coast.

dishes.name: Mulgikapsad
dishes.desc: Sauerkraut braised with pork and pearl barley, a hearty dish from Mulgimaa often called the national dish.

dishes.name: Vana Tallinn
dishes.desc: Dark sweet rum-based liqueur with vanilla, citrus and spices, drunk neat or in coffee.

dishes.name: Pastizzi
dishes.desc: Flaky diamond-shaped pastries filled with ricotta or mushy peas, sold hot at pastizzerias.

dishes.name: Rabbit Stew (Stuffat tal-Fenek)
dishes.desc: Rabbit braised in red wine, tomatoes and garlic, Malta's national dish served at fenkata feasts.

dishes.name: Lampuki Pie
dishes.desc: Pie of dolphinfish with spinach, olives, capers and tomatoes, baked in autumn during lampuki season.

dishes.name: Ftira
dishes.desc: Ring-shaped sourdough bread, split and filled with tuna, tomatoes, capers and olives.

dishes.name: Bragioli
dishes.desc: Thin beef slices rolled around a stuffing of bacon, egg and breadcrumbs, braised in tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Imqaret
dishes.desc: Diamond-shaped pastries filled with spiced dates, deep-fried and sold at street stalls.

dishes.name: Ħobż biż-Żejt
dishes.desc: Maltese bread rubbed with tomato and oil, topped with tuna, capers, olives and onions.

dishes.name: Timpana
dishes.desc: Baked pie of macaroni in meat sauce with eggs and cheese, encased in pastry.

dishes.name: Kinnie
dishes.desc: Bittersweet soft drink flavoured with bitter oranges and aromatic herbs.

dishes.name: Ġbejniet
dishes.desc: Small round sheep's-milk cheeselets eaten fresh, dried or peppered, from Malta and Gozo.

dishes.name: Aljotta
dishes.desc: Fish soup with garlic, tomatoes, rice and marjoram, finished with lemon.

dishes.name: Qassatat
dishes.desc: Round shortcrust pastries filled with ricotta or peas and onions.

dishes.name: Minestra
dishes.desc: Thick vegetable soup of pumpkin, potatoes, beans and pasta, the Maltese take on minestrone.

dishes.name: Kannoli Maltin
dishes.desc: Fried pastry tubes filled with sweetened ricotta, candied fruit and chocolate.

dishes.name: Ravjul
dishes.desc: Maltese square pasta parcels stuffed with sheep's-milk irkotta cheese and parsley, served with rich tomato and garlic sauce.

dishes.name: Bigilla
dishes.desc: Thick dip of mashed broad beans with garlic, chilli and herbs, served with galletti crackers.

dishes.name: Halloumi
dishes.desc: Firm brined cheese of goat's and sheep's milk that keeps its shape when grilled or fried.

dishes.name: Sheftalia
dishes.desc: Grilled sausages of minced pork and lamb with onion and parsley, wrapped in caul fat.

dishes.name: Souvlaki Kypriako
dishes.desc: Large chunks of pork grilled on long skewers, served in pitta with salad and lemon.

dishes.name: Meze
dishes.desc: Long sequence of small dishes, dips and grilled meats or fish shared over several hours.

dishes.name: Kleftiko (Cypriot)
dishes.desc: Lamb slow-baked with potatoes, garlic and herbs in a sealed clay oven.

dishes.name: Koupepia
dishes.desc: Vine leaves stuffed with minced pork, rice, tomato and herbs.

dishes.name: Loukoumades (Cypriot)
dishes.desc: Small fried dough balls soaked in honey or syrup and dusted with cinnamon.

dishes.name: Afelia
dishes.desc: Pork marinated in red wine and crushed coriander seeds, braised and served with bulgur.

dishes.name: Lountza
dishes.desc: Pork loin brined, marinated in red wine and smoked, often eaten in sandwiches with halloumi.

dishes.name: Zivania
dishes.desc: Clear pomace brandy distilled from grape residue and local dry wine.

dishes.name: Tavas
dishes.desc: Lamb or beef baked with onions, tomatoes and cumin in a clay pot.

dishes.name: Koupes
dishes.desc: Cigar-shaped bulgur shells stuffed with minced meat, onions and parsley, deep-fried.

dishes.name: Glyko Tou Koutaliou
dishes.desc: Fruit preserves in thick syrup, served on a spoon with water and coffee to welcome guests.

dishes.name: Trachanas
dishes.desc: Soup of dried cracked wheat fermented in sour milk, often served with halloumi.

dishes.name: Resi
dishes.desc: Wedding dish of wheat simmered slowly in chicken or lamb broth until thick and creamy.

dishes.name: Commandaria
dishes.desc: Sweet amber dessert wine from sun-dried grapes in the Troodos foothills, among the oldest named wines.

dishes.name: Tavë Kosi
dishes.desc: Baked lamb and rice under a thick layer of eggy yogurt, the national dish, originally from Elbasan.

dishes.name: Fërgesë
dishes.desc: Baked peppers, tomatoes and cottage cheese, sometimes with liver or veal, a Tirana speciality.

dishes.name: Byrek
dishes.desc: Filo pie filled with spinach, cheese, meat or leeks, sold at every bakery.

dishes.name: Flija
dishes.desc: Layers of crêpe-like batter brushed with cream, slow-baked under a hot lid covered in embers.

dishes.name: Qofte
dishes.desc: Grilled or fried meatballs of lamb or beef with mint and garlic, served with yogurt or fries.

dishes.name: Tavë Dheu
dishes.desc: Clay-pot bake of liver, peppers, tomatoes and cottage cheese, a Tirana speciality.

dishes.name: Speca të Mbushura
dishes.desc: Peppers stuffed with rice, herbs and minced meat, baked in tomato sauce.

dishes.name: Pispili
dishes.desc: Cornbread pie baked with leeks, spinach or wild greens and white cheese, from southern Albania.

dishes.name: Lakror
dishes.desc: Thin layered pie from Korçë filled with greens, leeks, onions or meat, cooked under a sač lid.

dishes.name: Trileçe
dishes.desc: Sponge cake soaked in three kinds of milk and topped with caramel, popular across Albania and Kosovo.

dishes.name: Ballokume
dishes.desc: Soft cornmeal and butter cookies from Elbasan, baked for the Summer Day festival in March.

dishes.name: Shëndetlie
dishes.desc: Honey and walnut cake soaked in syrup with cloves and cinnamon.

dishes.name: Petulla
dishes.desc: Fried dough puffs eaten for breakfast with honey, feta, jam or powdered sugar.

dishes.name: Raki
dishes.desc: Strong grape or mulberry brandy, offered to guests and drunk with meze.

dishes.name: Dhallë
dishes.desc: Salty yogurt drink diluted with water, served cold with grilled meats.

dishes.name: Japrakë
dishes.desc: Vine leaves stuffed with rice, herbs and sometimes minced meat.

dishes.name: Paçe Koke
dishes.desc: Rich soup of sheep's or calf's head with garlic and vinegar, eaten as a breakfast and hangover cure.

dishes.name: Kukurec
dishes.desc: Lamb intestines wrapped around offal and spit-roasted, a festive grill snack.

dishes.name: Fasule
dishes.desc: White bean stew with onions, tomato, paprika and mint, served with bread.

dishes.name: Sufllaqe
dishes.desc: Pita wrap of grilled pork or chicken with fries, tomatoes and tzatziki, the Albanian take on gyros.

dishes.name: Revani
dishes.desc: Semolina sponge cake soaked in lemon or orange syrup, served in squares with coffee.
